minutes.headline: Water commissioners and Hickory Hills landowners discussed the Hickory Hills well study and zone one bylaw wording; no vote taken.
minutes.summary: The commissioners met with Hickory Hills landowners' association representatives about a proposed pilot study of treating and pumping the Hickory Hills well. Disputes centered on proposed zone one bylaw wording that would remove boating and fishing, whether the district controls the lake area, and whether the district can sign a legal agreement with the landowners. Nothing was formally voted; the board agreed to seek DEP clarification and work with the landowners on study scope.

attendees.role: chairman of the board of commissioners

public_comment.stated_role: president of the hickory hills landowners
public_comment.topic: Landowners' representatives joined the discussion of the Hickory Hills well, and said they were disappointed to find well discussion in a town warrant that had not been raised with them.
Raised concerns about the zone one bylaw, DEP regulations on control of zone one, and the lack of a binding agreement limiting pumping.

budget_items.what_was_said: A speaker advised clarifying DEP's ownership and control requirements first so the district doesn't spend a large sum on a study that DEP could then block.
The superintendent said a new well can cost millions, and that the Hickory Hills well already represents a large investment.
The board noted legal counsel advises against agreements with a small group of residents because the district serves its whole customer base.
The board began by reviewing and signing the warrants.

decisions.decision: Agreed that DEP should be asked first to clarify ownership and control of zone one, including the land under the lake, before the pilot study proceeds.
The district will hold workshops with the landowners and share the study scope, and the engineering proposal will go to DEP for approval before bidding.
The board is not inclined to change the zone one bylaw wording itself, saying the public can amend it at town meeting, though commissioners later said they dislike the wording.

what_happened.line: No vote was taken; commissioners agreed DEP should be asked first to clarify ownership and control of zone one, including the land under the lake.
The district will hold workshops with Hickory Hills landowners, share the study scope, and send the engineering proposal to DEP for approval before bidding.
The board said it is not inclined to change the zone one bylaw wording itself, noting the public can amend it at town meeting.
Legal counsel advises against agreements with a small group of residents, so a binding agreement with the landowners was left unresolved.
Landowners' representatives raised concerns about the zone one bylaw, DEP rules on control of zone one, and the lack of a binding limit on pumping.

why_it_matters: The pilot study of treating and pumping the Hickory Hills well cannot start until DEP weighs in, so any spending on the study, and any later cost of a replacement well, depends on that answer.
The zone one bylaw wording, which landowners say would remove boating and fishing, is a question residents may be asked to amend at town meeting.
